full_judgment:
Md Imman Ali J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 2-4-2018 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6298 of 2010 discharge the Rule. 

 2. The fact of the case in brief are that the petitioner Md Solim Ullah lodged an FIR on 10-7-2009 with Lohagora Police Station naming Md Nurul Alam alias Nurul Amin and seven other accused persons who were alleged to have committed an officer under sections 399/402 of the Penal Code thus giving rise to Lohagora PS Case No.06 dated 10-7-2009. After investigation, the police submitted police report (final report) No. 19 dated 18-7-2009 recommending discharge of the accused as there was no prima facie evidence against them. The police also sought permission to take legal action against the informant under section 211 of the Penal Code. 

 3. The informant of that case filed a naraji petition dated 30-7-2009 against the prayer for discharging the accused and prayer for re-investigation of the case by a different investigating agency. By his order dated 12-8-2009 against the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate upon considering the statements of witnesses recorded under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code) as well as the naraji petition, accepted the final report, discharged the accused named in the FIR rejected the naraji petition and granted permission to take steps against the informant under section 211 of the Penal Code. 

 4. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the order dated 12-8-2009, the petitioner filed Criminal Revision Case No. 222/09 before the Sessions Judge, Chattogram. The petitioner's revisional application is not before us, but from the order dated 26-8-2009 rejecting the same, it appears that the petitioner simply challenged the rejection of the naraji petition. 

 5. Challenging the judgment and order of the Sessions Judge, Chattogram dated 26-8-2009, the petitioner filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6298 of 2010, before the High Court Division, under section 561A of the Code, whereupon Rule was issued. 

 6. It may be mentioned here that the Investigating Officer of Lohagora Police Station Case No.06 dated 10-7-2009, lodged FIR No. 16 dated 18-7-2009 against Md Solim Ullah and 3 others alleging an office under section 19A of the Arms Act. In due course, after investigation police submitted charge sheet against four persons including Md Solim Ullah. The case was then transferred to Special Tribunal No. 1, Chattogram and numbered as Special Tribunal Case No. 77 of 2009. When the case was fixed for charge hearing, the accused filed an application for discharge under section 241A of the Code, but the Tribunal framed charged against them under section 19A of the Arms Act upon rejecting their application for discharge by order dated 10-6-2010. The accused then filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.24579 of 2010 under section 561A of the Code before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. 

 7. After hearing, both the Rules were discharged by the impugned judgment. Hence, Md Solim Ullah has filed the instant criminal petition for leave to appeal specifically challenging the discharge of the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6298 of 2010. However, a specific ground has also been urged in respect of discharge of the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 24579 of 2010. 

 11. Thus section 195(1) (b) of the Code, so far as it is relevant for this case, provides that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 211 of the Penal Code when such offence is alleged to have been committed in, or in relation to, any proceeding in any Court, except on the complaint in writing of such Court. 

 "476. Procedure in cases mentioned in section 195—(1) When any Civil, Revenue or Criminal Court is, whether on application made to it in this behalf or otherwise, of opinion that it is expedient in the interests of justice that an inquiry should be made into any offence referred to in section 195, sub-section (1), clause (b) or clause (c), which appears to have been committed in or in relation to a proceeding in that Court, such Court may, after such preliminary inquiry, if any, as it thinks necessary, record a finding to that effect and make a complaint thereof in writing signed by the presiding office of the Court, and shall forward the same to a Magistrate of the first class having jurisdiction 

 13. An essential component of section 195(1)(b) read with section 476(1) is that the offence mentioned in section 195(1)(b), which includes section 211 of the Penal Code, must have been committed in or in relation to a proceeding in that Court. And in that event prosecution under section 211 would have to be initiated upon a complaint in writing by the Presiding Officer of the Court under section 195(1)(b) of the Code and then forwarded to a Magistrate of the first class having jurisdiction as provided by section 476 of the Code. The earlier view of the High Court Division as appears from the decision in the case of Haji Abdus Samad, vs Haji lobed Ali alias Haji Abdul Jabbar, 28 DLR 58 was that when in any case the police files final report against the accused named in the FIR there is no proceeding existing they had been discharged, and the naraji petition was rejected. That decision was followed by the High Court Division in a later decision in the case of Abdul Quader vs Serajuddowla, 8 BLD 517 = 38 DLR 321. However, on appeal before this Division Serajuddowla vs Abdul Kader, (reported in 13 BLD (AD) 94) = 45 DLR (AD) 101 his Lordship ATM Afzal, J as his Lordship was then, by reference to the case of Abdur Rahman vs State, reported in 29 DLR (SC) 256, observed that: 

 Their Lordships held in the Seraj-ud-dowla case that a Magistrate acts in his judicial capacity while discharging an accused on the basis of a final report submitted by the police and that the offence under section 211 of the Penal Code was allegedly committed by the appellant of that case in relation to a proceeding in Court and, as such, the bar under section 195(1)(b) of the Code is attracted, and therefore a complaint by the presiding Officer of the Court is necessary." 

 14. In the above mentioned case of Abdul Quader vs Serajuddowla and others the police had submitted a final report with a note which read as follows: "Forwarded FR is false under sections 147/448/380 BPC Sanction for prosecuting the complainant under section 211 BPC may kindly be accorded." 

 "Seen the final report (false) under section 147/448/380 of the Penal Code and it is accepted. Accused persons are discharged from the case. The Investigation Officer in the final report has prayed for prosecuting the informant under section 211 of the Penal Code. Heard. Let the informant be prosecuted under section 211 of the Penal Code, as prayed for." 

 "Therefore, this is not a case in which a private complaint has been lodged after the submission of the final report by the Police and discharge of the accused thereon nor is it a case where the police of its own motion have started the prosecution against the appellant. It is clear from the facts of the present case that the prosecution of the appellant was sanctioned by the Magistrate himself and, as such, it could not be said that the cognizance has been taken in violation of section 195(1) (b) of the Code. In view of the discussion above, this appeal is dismissed." 

 19. In the instant case by order dated 12-8-2019 the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, Chattogram upon consideration of the materials before him accepted the final report and acceded to the prayer of the Investigation Officer to prosecute the informant Md Solim Ullah and others to take steps in accordance with law under section 211 of the Penal Code. Md Solim Ullah then filed revisional application before the Sessions Jude, Chattogram which was numbered as Criminal Revisional Case No. 222 of 2009 under sections 435/436/ 439A of the Code. In due course the learned Sessions Judge, Chattogram by his order dated 26-8-2009 summarily rejected the revisional application. Md Solim Ullah then filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.6298 of 2010 before the High Court Division challenging the order of the Sessions Judge, Chattogram by which his application for reinvestigation was rejected. It appears that no issue was raised either before the Sessions Judge, Chattogram or before the High Court Division with regard to the permission granted by the learned Senior Judicial Magistrate for the police to prosecute 

 24. It appears that the point of law which arose in the case of Serajuddowla mentioned above is the same as the instant case, although the point of law raised before us was not raised earlier before the subordinate Courts or the High Court Division. The final decision in that case was against the petitioner, i.e. the case was allowed to proceed since the police started a Non-GR case. However, with respect, we cannot agree with decision in the Serajuddowla case that the provisions of section 195(1) (b) had been complied with, since in our view permission of the police to take steps to prosecute under section 211 of the Penal Code cannot be termed as a "complaint" within the meaning of section 195(1) (b) read with section 4(1) (h) of the Code, which in fact has to be made to a Magistrate. 

 25. Now let us consider what was actually before the High Court Division in the instant case. The criminal petition for leave to appeal now before us, on the face of it seeks to challenge the judgment and order of discharge the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 6298 of 2010. Mysteriously the petition before us does not provide the facts and details of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 24579 of 2010 which was heard and disposed of by the same judgment and order. However, one ground was taken in the instant petition that the Special Tribunal without considering the prosecution materials illegally framed charge against the petitioners under section 19A of the Arms Act and hence the proceedings should be quashed under section 561A of the Code. 

 26. We find from the records of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 24579 of 2010 that out of the self-same occurrence a separate FIR was lodged against the same accused being Lohagora Police Station Case No. 7 dated 10-7- 2019 under section 19A of the Arms Act. Police investigated both Police Station Case No. 6 and 7 dated 10-7-2019 together and submitted final report in both cases. A separate police report (final report) was submitted in the arms case being police report No. 09- 6478/2 dated 18-7-2019 which was placed before the Special Tribunal in Special Tribunal Case No. 64/09, recommending discharge of the accused. The police officer, namely SI Mostafa Kamal Sarker who had investigated Lohagora Police Station Case No. 6(7)09 and No. 7(7)09 and submitted final report in both cases, then recorded FIR No. 16 dated 18-7-2009 under section 19A of the Arms Act against Md Solim Ullah the informant of the earlier case as well as 3 others. In due course, after investigation charge sheet was submitted against Md Solim Ullah and three other accused alleging offence under section 19A of the Arms Act. Then the case was transferred to the Special Tribunal No.1, Chattogram where it was numbered as Special Tribunal Case No.77 of 2009. Thereafter, the case was transferred to Special Tribunal No. 13, Chattogram where charge was framed against the petitioner (Md Solim Ullah) and 3 others under section 19 A of the Arms Act upon rejecting their application filed under section 241A of the Code. The petitioner and 3 other accused then filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.24579 of 2010 under section 561A of the Code. 

 27. It is noted that the case now pending against the petitioner is the arms case which was started on 18-7-2009 i.e. before the order dated 12-8-2009 by which the petitioner was permitted to be prosecuted under section 211 of the Penal Code. Hence the FIR in the arms case was not the result of the order dated 12-8-2009 and is in every respect lawful and there is no question of the application of the bar of section 195(1) (b) of the Code. 

 29. There is nothing on record to show that any prosecution has been started under section 211 of the Penal Code. In view of the case against the petitioner under section 19A of the Arms Act, prosecution under section 211 of the Penal Code is unlikely in any event. The argument advanced by Mr Shahjahan is nothing more than just a pre-emptive measure and an attempt to pull the wool over the Court's eyes. 

 30. Due to the two criminal miscellaneous petitions filed before the High Court Division, the arms case pending against the petitioner and others has been kept in cold storage for more than nine years. This delay caused by the use of section 561A of the Code is the result of an abuse of the process of the Court and defeats delivery of justice. 

 31. We reiterate that applications invoking section 561A of the Code should not he so readily entertained, especially when the end result would be to delay and defeat the ends of justice. In the instant case there are specific allegations against the accused. Delaying the trial, particularly on technical ground, result in the erosion of public confidence in the justice delivery system. In this regard we may refer to the decision of the Indian Supreme Court in the case of State of HP vs Lekh Raj, 2000 SCC (Crl) 147 where it was observed as follows:—
